case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The SJC held that a trial judge's subsidiary findings stand unless clearly erroneous but the appellate court independently reviews whether those findings establish parental unfitness by clear and convincing evidence, and it reversed the Juvenile Court judgment placing the children in the department's permanent custody.
key_cases.relevance: Where the proof falls short of clear and convincing evidence of unfitness, the custody judgment must be reversed and the children returned.
key_cases.quote: although the judge’s findings were not clearly erroneous, the evidence on which they were based did not prove parental unfitness by clear and convincing evidence

key_cases.holding: The SJC held that on a petition for review and redetermination under G. L. c. 119, § 26, the moving party bears only an initial burden of producing credible evidence of changed circumstances, after which the department must prove by clear and convincing evidence that the child is still in need of care and protection; the burden may never be shifted to the parent.
key_cases.relevance: A child is discharged from the department's custody when the department can no longer carry its clear-and-convincing burden that the child remains in need of care and protection.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that in a petition for review and redetermination, the department bears the ultimate burden to prove that the child is still in need of care and protection

key_cases.holding: The SJC held that where a Juvenile Court awards "permanent" custody of a nonmarital child to the father in a care and protection case, the Juvenile Court may keep the case open until a Probate and Family Court judge enters a custody order under G. L. c. 209C, and that this practice satisfies due process.
key_cases.relevance: A motion to dismiss and close the care and protection case was properly denied until the parallel c. 209C custody order was in place.
key_cases.quote: We agree that this practice best reflects the Legislature's intent and harmonizes the two statutory schemes.

key_cases.holding: The SJC held that parents in a care and protection proceeding are entitled to the effective assistance of appointed counsel, measured by the criminal-law Saferian standard, but affirmed because the department proved unfitness by clear and convincing evidence and the ineffectiveness claim was not properly raised below.
key_cases.relevance: A parent who shows constitutionally ineffective counsel may obtain relief from the resulting custody judgment, but ordinarily must raise the claim below rather than for the first time on appeal.
key_cases.quote: Accordingly, we conclude that parents are entitled to the effective assistance of counsel pursuant to G. L. c. 119, § 29.

key_cases.holding: The SJC affirmed the denial of the children's Mass. R. Civ. P. 60(b)(6) motion for a new trial, holding that the Saferian standard governs ineffective-assistance claims in care and protection proceedings, that counsel's joint representation of siblings created no actual conflict and no prejudice was shown given overwhelming proof of the father's unfitness, and directing that counsel for children follow the 1999 CPCS performance standards on representing a child's expressed preferences.
key_cases.relevance: A child dissatisfied with the resulting custody judgment may seek relief under rule 60(b)(6), but must show both deficient representation and prejudice before the judgment will be undone.
key_cases.quote: their positions, based on mature expression, are entitled to weight in custody proceedings (although not determinative)
